newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas closes up on technicals, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas closes up on technicals, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures mostly ended higher Thursday in fairly active trade, helped by technical buying and reports of firmer physical prices as May flows began, industry sources said.
June gained 5.9 cents to close at $2.243 per million British thermal units. July settled 5.7 cents higher at $2.261. Most others ended up by 1.8 to 5.1 cents.

"Cash was up a couple of cents but not enough to support this move. There was a lot of technical upside on NYMEX today, but not a lot of hard information," said one East Coast trader, noting June's move above $2.24 triggered chart buying.

Despite prospects for steady storage demand this month, most remained skeptical current prices will be sustained without broader cooling loads. While parts of Texas and the West are expected to heat up next week, most other regions were forecast at seasonal to below-seasonal temperatures.
And while the technical picture looked constructive, chart watchers said the market was overbought and due for a correction after an eight percent rally in three days amid rising open interest.
They pegged next resistance in June in the $2.33 area and then at the $2.385 contract high. Support was seen at $2.05 and then along the up trendline at $2.01.

In the cash, Gulf Coast swing prices firmed a couple of cents Thursday to the mid-teens. Midcon pipes were up about a nickel to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also gained five cents to the mid-$2.40s.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip rose 4.5 cents to $2.307.

On the KCBT, June finished 6.3 cents higher at $2.08, while deferreds ended up by one to five cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.4 cent to 16.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 875 lots changed hands, up sharply from Wednesday's total of 372.
